analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol in the third person masculine singular. The singular verb precedes the compound subject Abram and Nahor.

article.name: שָׂרַי
article.summary: Sarai is the name by which Abram’s wife is introduced. Her later name שָׂרָה has the same form as the Hebrew noun for a princess or noblewoman, supporting a similar meaning for Sarai. The text leaves the force of the earlier name’s ending unexplained.

analysis.evidence: The first clause gives Sarai as the name of Abram’s wife. The second repeats the same construction for Nahor’s wife, with מִלְכָּה supplying her name.
analysis.morphology: וְ is the conjunction “and.” שֵׁם is a masculine singular common noun in construct, heading the chain שֵׁם אֵשֶׁת נָחוֹר, “the name of Nahor’s wife.”
